## Finish

_Congratulations! You've completed the DHCP course! :tada:_

<img src="https://octodex.github.com/images/welcometocat.png" alt=celebrate width=300 align=right>

### Here's a recap of what you learned:

- **DHCP Fundamentals**: Understood the DORA process (Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge)
- **Server Configuration**: Configured an ISC DHCP server with scopes, lease times, and DNS settings
- **Lease Management**: Created static reservations for devices using MAC addresses
- **Troubleshooting**: Built a diagnostic toolkit for common DHCP issues

### Key Takeaways

| Concept | Summary |
|---------|--------|
| DORA | The 4-step handshake every DHCP lease starts with |
| Scope | The IP range your server manages |
| Reservation | Static IP tied to a device's MAC address |
| Lease Time | How long a client holds an IP before renewal |
| Port 67/68 | DHCP server (67) and client (68) UDP ports |

### Additional Learning Resources

- [RFC 2131 - DHCP Specification](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2131)
- [ISC DHCP Server Documentation](https://www.isc.org/dhcp/)
- [Linux DHCP Client (`dhclient`) man page](https://linux.die.net/man/8/dhclient)
- [Windows DHCP Server Guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/technologies/dhcp/dhcp-top)
- [Wireshark DHCP Analysis](https://www.wireshark.org/)

### What's Next?

- Study **DNS** to understand how hostnames resolve to IP addresses
- Learn **VLANs** and DHCP relay agents for multi-subnet networks
- Explore **DHCPv6** for IPv6 address assignment
- Practice with **Wireshark** to capture and analyze DHCP traffic
